Hi Daniel / CardioMed security team,

Thanks again for taking the call today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary from today's demo
- Primary ask: customer-managed keys for patient PHI at rest (BYOK) and auditability of KMS operations.
- Compliance drivers: SOC 2 Type II coverage, HIPAA considerations for patient-data-bearing workloads, and GDPR data-residency concerns for EU records.
- Preferred model: CardioMed wants an HSM-backed CMK option with clear non-exportability and per-tenant key separation.

What Redwood can provide (high level)
- BYOK options: AWS/KMS-interop + HSM-backed CMKs (FIPS 140-2/3 vendor integrations), or bring-your-own-HSM via KMIP connectors for on-prem HSMs.
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ enforced; per-connection mTLS for private deployments.
- At-rest: AES-256-GCM recommended; we offer KM encryption and per-tenant key isolation.
- Auditability: detailed KMS operation logs routed to a customer-controlled logging sink; we can deliver audit exports for QSA review.

Attachments: [attachment: redwood-cmk-intake-form.xlsx (xlsx, 28 KB)] — please complete the intake form so our security team can kick off the technical intake and QSA packet.

Proposed next steps
1) Please confirm which data classes (PHI subsets) need CMK protection and whether EU residency applies.
2) Complete intake form by EOD 2026-11-09.
3) Redwood to share SOC 2 coverage summary and a technical KMS configuration doc (attached by Rishi on follow-up).
4) Schedule a QSA-intake meeting w/ your compliance team the week of 11/12 — suggested 11/12 or 11/13 (PT).

If you prefer, we can route the intake as a HubSpot board item (I included a link in the metadata).

Thanks — I looped Rishi and Monica for the technical and compliance follow-up.

Ava — thanks for the recap. Couple of clarifying questions from our security/legal leads: 

1) SOC 2: Do you have a Type II report we can review (even a redacted version)? Which Trust Services Criteria are in scope (CC1-CC7)?
2) Encryption at rest: what algorithms/modes are used by default? We need explicit confirmation AES-256-GCM or equivalent.
3) HSM: Can you confirm FIPS level (140-2 vs 140-3) and whether keys marked as non-exportable can be enforced when Redwood runs in hosted mode?
4) BYOK flow: we run an on-prem HSM and want a technical summary of the KMIP/connector flow — is there an option where our HSM holds the root key and Redwood holds ephemeral operational keys?
5) Key rotation & revocation: what are typical rotation intervals/automations and what happens to existing ciphertext if a key is rotated or revoked?
6) Evidence: any pen-test summary, SOC 2 scope doc, or prior customer reference that covers KMS controls would help accelerate legal review.

We may have a short list of mandatory clauses for the DPA — I'll loop Legal after we get the SOC 2 and KMS details.

Thanks,

Daniel — answers inline below. Quoted your questions for context.

> 1) SOC 2: Do you have a Type II report we can review (even a redacted version)? Which Trust Services Criteria are in scope (CC1-CC7)?
Yes — Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report covering Availability and Confidentiality controls mapped across CC1-CC7. We can provide a redacted report and a SOC 2 coverage summary for KMS-specific controls. Attached: [attachment: SOC2-summary.pdf (pdf, 94 KB)].

> 2) Encryption at rest: what algorithms/modes are used by default? We need explicit confirmation AES-256-GCM or equivalent.
Default at-rest encryption uses AES-256-GCM for object/key-encryption paths. For block-level protections we leverage AES-256-GCM with integrity checks. TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 recommended) for all in-transit traffic.

> 3) HSM: Can you confirm FIPS level (140-2 vs 140-3) and whether keys marked as non-exportable can be enforced when Redwood runs in hosted mode?
We integrate with FIPS 140-2 and FIPS 140-3 validated HSM vendors (YubiHSM, Thales, etc.). When using HSM-backed CMKs in hosted mode, keys can be configured as non-exportable and enforced by the HSM provider; Redwood's runtime will never expose key material. We can document the specific HSM validation IDs for your vendor review.

> 4) BYOK flow: we run an on-prem HSM and want a technical summary of the KMIP/connector flow — is there an option where our HSM holds the root key and Redwood holds ephemeral operational keys?
Yes — two supported patterns:
- Hybrid: CardioMed maintains a root/master key in your on-prem HSM; we perform an envelope-key operation where a derived key (wrapped by your root) is used by the runtime. Your root never leaves your HSM; wrapped keys are non-exportable by policy.
- Pure KMIP connector: Redwood can connect to your KMIP endpoint (customer-managed) for live operations. Latency and availability trade-offs apply; we can run a small PoC to measure performance.

> 5) Key rotation & revocation: what are typical rotation intervals/automations and what happens to existing ciphertext if a key is rotated or revoked?
We recommend 90-day rotation for keys protecting high-sensitivity PHI, but policy can be customer-defined. Rotation creates a new CMK version; existing ciphertext remains decryptable as long as older key versions are retained per your retention policy. Revocation prevents future decrypt operations; we log all attempts and can provide audit exports.

> 6) Evidence: any pen-test summary, SOC 2 scope doc, or prior customer reference that covers KMS controls would help accelerate legal review.
Attached: [attachment: SOC2-summary.pdf (pdf, 94 KB)] and [attachment: KMS-configuration-guide.pdf (pdf, 212 KB)]. We also maintain a short pen-test executive summary we can share under NDA — happy to surface that in the DocuSign NDA.

Additional notes:
- Audit trails: we can stream key-operation logs to an S3-compatible endpoint or your SIEM; logs include operation, principal, timestamp, request/response identifiers.
- Data residency: for EU records we can pin hosting to an EU region and use a customer-managed key in that region.
- Access controls: RBAC + MFA enforced for key admin operations; separate token-based access for runtime.

If this looks good I'll prep the QSA intake packet and coordinate dates for the intake call.
